November, 1992     Page Reply

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Mervyn Toogood, BRISTOL


Dear Brian,

I have written to a couple of
various clubs for help before I
became a member of OUTLET but
"no joy" in reference to a
reply. I feel sure it will not
happen when writing to you.

I have a Spectrum +3 and Epson
LX-400 printer. Can I get a
printout of the contents page,
and how?

Thanking you in anticipation.

        Mervyn Toogood

Brian Cavers to Mervyn Toogood

To print a copy of the OUTLET
CONTENTS page on the +3 version:

1. RESET

2. Enter MERGE "CONTENTS"

3. Wait a few seconds until
   "O.K." appears.

4. Press the ENTER key.

5. Type: 26 COPY then press
   the ENTER key.

6. Type: RUN then press ENTER.

Disciple/+D users load the usual
way; use SAVE SCREEN$ instead of
COPY (or the snap button).

SAM users should first load the
DUMP code or MASTERBASIC and
then use DUMP instead of COPY.

Other users will need their own
dump software. If you enter...

     SAVE "CONSCRN" SCREEN$

       ...at line 26 then you
could save the CONTENTS screen
and load it into any program
that will print a screen.

                       - Brian

From: G. Caldwell, LONDONDERRY



Dear Ron,

I've a problem with my MX 80/FT
printer. I recently pulled out
the printer lead from the back
of the Spectrum. Everything
worked normally on one occasion
afterwards, but after that
nothing would print from the
Spectrum.

I use Tasword+3 and the Multi-
face 3 for screen dumps. These
have been working perfectly for
3 years. Now they are dead. The
Spectrum does not seem to be
communicating with the printer.

I connected up another +3
computer which I knew worked
with the MX 80 before, but the
result was the same: nothing.

I also have a 486 DX 25 MHZ PC,
in fact I have typed this letter
on it. The printer is, as you
can see, working perfectly with
this computer.

What is wrong? Have codes been
upset, either in the printer or
the +3 computer? Please help if
you can;I would be most grateful
as I use Tasword+3 all the time.

       Yours faithfully,

        George Caldwell

Brian Cavers to George Caldwell


The common factor is the cable.
It seems highly likely that when
you pulled out the cable then a
connection in the connector was
broken. You could open it up and
resolder it or, if you do not
know how or know of a friend who
can do it for you, buy a new
cable. It would possibly even be
cheaper than getting the present
cable repaired commercially and
less hassle.

                        - Brian

From: B. Edgeway, NORWICH

Dear Brian,

Thank you for your replies in
October's edition of oUTLET.

I print labels for my homemade
wine. The first part is graphics
of a bottle and a glass. The
second part you can enter the
name of the wine and various
other bits of information (it's
quite good even though I say so
myself). The problem is the
first part, the graphics have to
be SAVEd as a screen$, and as a
result when the printer has
finished with the graphics, it
carries on rolling down onto the
next label as the empty part of
the screen.

At this point I "stop" the
program, wind the printer back
to the next label and "RUN" it
again until I have the required
amount of labels, at which point
the second part of the program
takes place which is no problem.

I can program a SCREEN$ to show
what part of the screen I want
displayed but do you know how I
can program a SCREEN$ dump to
the printer to stop printing at
a point I desire instead of the
whole screen?

If that is not possible, is
there an escape routine that I
can program the printer to
reverse to my desired position.
I do not seem to have mastered
escape routines on my printer -

they do not seem to work. If the
above is possible I could print
as many labels as I needed in
one go instead of having to stop
and start after each one.

My printer is a STAR LC 10 col-
our and I have a Spectrum 128+2
with a +D interface.

Do you know of a routine that I
can use to print a screen dump
in the screen colours? I have
tried all sorts of ways to do
this but have not yet succeeded,
or will I have to resort to
purchasing a printer driver as
advertised by Datel?

How can I program a cheat into a
game on disc SAVEd as a snap
file? It's the LOAD code part

that I think is the problem, as
if it's a cheat on tape you use
load""code, but on disc to LOAD
you use LOAD d1"game"s for a 48k
game but you cannot use code
with that?

Any ideas please?

        Yours sincerely,

          Barry Edgeway

Brian Cavers to Barry Edgeway

We've two programs in the pipe-
line that dump selected lines of
the screen. One is for 9-pin
printers and the other is for
24-pin printers.They will appear
in a future OUTLET. They also
have other features like density
options. The 9-pin program is
called "SCOPY" and the 24-pin
program is "HARD24.2" so look
out for them, I hope, soon.

Meanwhile, if your printer does
accept the reverse line feed
command(see your printer manual)
then use POKE @6,1 : LPRINT (the
reverse line feed code). I have
several lists of codes but can't
find this one.

Note that the above are not in
colour. Special software is
needed for colour dumps. If you
like dabbling in BASIC you could
examine BASDUMP in OUTLET 45 in
conjunction with your printer
manual to see if it could be
adapted to dump colour but it
would always be slow.

We have never had a colour dump
program in OUTLET so, failing
that, you will have to buy the
Datel one. The latest advert I
have lists it at `19.99 from
Datel Electronics, Govan Road,
Fenton Industrial Estate,
Fenton, Stoke on Trent, ST4 2RS.

I wish we did have a nice colour
dump machine code routine in
OUTLET!

That is a nice project for some
machine code enthusiast who also
has a colour printer! We'll be
glad to publish it in OUTLET! I
would not think that it would be
too difficult - possibly less
than a greyscale dump.

I have a good excuse not to try
this myself - I don't have a
colour printer so I would be
working blindly - even if I had
details of the printer colour
command codes! It's very, very
difficult to program that way!

Ron has written a program to do
cheats on snapshots and I will
try to get it in OUTLET soon.

                        - Brian

From: Brian Gaff, B.G. SERVICES,
 64, Roebuck Road, CHESSINGTON,
         Surrey, KT9 1JX

In David Burke's letter he
comments that BETA BASIC will
not work on his +2. I seem to
recall an article by John Wase
in Format in which he was run-
ning this on a +2. It will NOT
run on the +2A however, without
my mod kit. (sorry about the
plug!). This is due to the way
the RAM/RAM paging has been
changed.

With regard to OPENTYPE files on
the +D, I think the main reason
for using them is that you can
handle files much bigger than
the RAM you have left!

I had a Multiprint briefly, and
it was capable of emulating the
Kempston E, as I recall.

Yes, the +2 Ramdisc is an odd
device. It seems to dynamically
divide the available space be-
tween directory and files. This
would explain the odd results
obtained by Mr Miles. There is
also the second screen, of
course, and it is a known bug
that no check is made on dir-
ectory usage so it's possible to
overwrite this when lots of
little files are SAVEd. There is
a lot more info available in the
sysvars that CAT gives. Perhaps
Ron or I should send Chris
Oliver a copy of the Lunter
Emulator!

I agree with Malcolm Perry about
Graham Scarr. I saw him selling
new +3s for `55 a few months ago
-You don't mind learning Spanish
to read the manual, do you?

I have been helping someone with
a Disciple to get it going on
his +3. He has now managed it,
he says, and will no doubt be in
touch as he is an OUTLET reader.

By the way, those who have got
PCs lying around might be un-
aware of an interesting fact.
Tasman Software do a TASWORD for
the PC! It's very like TASWORD 3
to use,and I got used to it very
quickly. It's true to say that
better products exist, but it is
not a several hundred pound
touch like most of these! -Brian

From: Dominic Morris, MALVERN:

Many thank for another excellent
OUTLET (Issue 62). However, I
have to have a moan, so here
goes. In 'SOLVEX',if a quadratic
(or any equation with x to the
power n where n is greater than
1) only one answer is prodced.
Try x squared equals 4; it
produces the answer 2 when it
should be plus or minus 2.

I haven't solved that problem
but I have solved the +3 BIM-BAM
bug, it should also crash on the
+2A. Figured it out yet? Yes,
it's our old friend (?) the lazy
programmer. Tanod has used the
ROM vector-table. So. after 5
minutes work, I've come up with
the following solution...

Add the line...

8850 POKE 46084,148: FOR N=37888
 TO 37888+256:POKE N,255:NEXT N
              ...and you'll have
a fully-functioning demo.

I've just bought a DISCIPLE and
thanks to BG Services I've got
it working on my +3. I therefore
hope that you won't drop any
+D/DISCIPLE programs from the +3
version of OUTLET.

I was dismayed by the news of an
increase in the price of OUTLET,
but if it is to ensure its
future publication then I have
no complaints.

Best wishes and keep up the good
work.          - Dominic Morris

Brian Cavers to Dominic Morris

Thanks for solving the BIM BAM
bug.

All Spectrum versions of OUTLET
include the same programs so if
anyone switches to another sys-
tem they can use programs off
another version. You may have to
occasionally change some syntax.

                        - Brian

From: R.R. Grimmer, WIRRAL

Dear Ron and Brian,

I am sorry I have not used a
TASWORD file or even 'JOTTER'
but I typed half this letter
twice on both set-ups and on
each occasion I 'lost' the
script - hence this hand written
note. I am not use to the
'TASWORD 2' system and in the
case of 'JOTTER' I LOADed from
EXTRA 1 and when I reached the
bottom of the screen the script
would neither go up or down but
locked up with no prompt or
cursor in sight. I have no idea
what went wrong, because I
followed everything to the
letter!


May I ask your guidance in
utilising 'OUTLET EXTRA 1'.I've
tried to use 'COL 80+' and also
'OUTPRINT' but when the menu
appears and a selection is made,
or a file name is used, I enter
the selection, but in reply I
get "Invalid file name 290:4".
In fact when I wish to copy
(print) any OUTLET items I
select Kempson E but the screen
locks up.

I have selected ZX or LPrint III
and end up with a poor
reproduction with each line
preceded by a ? mark.

I admit to being quite vague in
the utilisation of a printer. I
do wish to utilise the full
width of the paper when printing

on A4 single sheets, but up to
now I have not been very
successful.

My set-up consists of the STAR
L10 mk II printer; Spectrums 48+
and 128K; Disciple and +D
interfaces; 5 1/4" and 3 1/2"
DDDS disc drives. Although the 5
1/4" drive has been acting up
lately with the loss of about
ten discs through track errors,
despite cleaning the drive. So,
any help you can offer me would
be very much appreciated. Mean-
time, do keep up the good work.
OUTLET is very beneficial to a
'non' programmer like me (70
years) who prefers the benefits
derived from more skilled and
dedicated people like yourselves
and others.

My very best wishes to you all
and good luck with your varying
problems in your quest to main-
tain an excellent 'Disczine'.

       Yours sincerely,

      R.R. Grimmer (Dick)

Brian Cavers to Dick Grimmer

Firstly, in JOTTER, note the bit
in the instructions about each
DATA statement starting a new
paragraph. To put it the other
way, you must start a new DATA
statement on a new line each
time you start a new paragraph.
The Spectrum will not let you
(easily) enter text in a BASIC
line that is larger than the
screen area so the largest
paragraph you can have is one
screen page.

In Tasword 2, just hold down the
symbol key and press the A key
to return to the menu where you
can select the SAVE TEXT option.
You will find Tasword easier to
use than JOTTER.

If you have the tape version of
Tasword 2 then it will only save
the text to tape - not to disc.
The prompt will say something
like"START THE TAPE,PRESS A KEY"
or suchlike. In that case you
need to change the SAVE syntax
to save to disc. Let me know if
you need any help with this. If
you are loading Tasword from +D
disc however, it seems likely it
has already been altered.

If you still have difficulties,
write again and give me more
detail of how far you get and
any errors you see.

The problem with loading text in
COL 80+ and OUTPRINT is due to
the following...

Early OUTLET text files had a
Sinclair keyword token added at
the end called "CODE". This is
really a single character that
the Spectrum expands into the
full word "CODE" just as when
you type in 48K BASIC the word
appears if you press "I" in
extended mode and you can then
move the cursor back and forth
over the whole word - it does
not go through letter by letter
as it would in 128K mode.

To enter the keyword "CODE" in a
filename you can press "I" in
extended mode in the input (even
in 128K mode).

Later issues of OUTLET use ".#"
instead so you need to CAT and
enter the name shown.

I do not know if you can print
using the Kempston E if you also
have a Disciple or +D attached.I
would expect it to fail.Have you
successfully used it in any
other software? Are you able to
simply enter LPRINT"TESTING" and
get it to print through the
Kempston E? If not then you will
need to cable a BBC-type printer
cable and print using your +D or
Disciple printer port(select the
Disciple option on-screen).

The normal Spectrum page print
from OUTLET is in 32 columns. To
print more widely using the
TABLOID option.

                      - Brian

From: Miles Kinloch, Flat 16,
      6 Drummond Street,
      EDINBURGH  EH8 9TU

Dear Brian,

First of all, many thanks for
sending me the rest of the ROM
Index files. I now have my +D,
and what a pleasure it was to
use OUTLET on disk. It's great
to be able to select any item at
random from the Contents page.

One of the things that had put
me off getting a +D until now
had been its reputation for not
working well in conjunction with
other interfaces, and as I have
several add-ons in my set-up, I
was fearful of having to give up
most, if not all, of them.

In all, I now have a Multiface,
Videoface, Two-Face (with the +D
in the upright position) and be-
hind that a Currah Microslot in-
to which are plugged a Kempston
Mouse interface and a Protek/
Kempston Joystick interface. And
to cap it all, the mouse inter-
face attaches via a short ribbon
cable (about 1 inch), something
which even the +D manual itself
warns may upset its operation.

Imagine my surprise, nay, aston-
ishment when I discovered that
all the above worked perfectly
happily when connected together
on my own machine (grey +2) - no
problems whatever that I can
detect.

I suppose the explanation has to
be that tolerances must vary
widely from model to model, as I
have heard of cases of Spectrums
becoming overloaded with even
just two peripherals. I must be
one of the lucky ones, I guess.

Your comment about character
arrays being LOADed without a
DIM puzzled me at first, as I'd
never been able to get this to
work - until now,that is,when I
tried it in 48K mode. It seems
if a character array is LOADed
in 128K mode without a DIM, it
LOADs but is corrupted, so this
must be yet another peculiarity
of 128K BASIC that's come to
light. (I'd always assumed 48K
was the same). I wonder if the
+3 also has this bug?

While I was experimenting I made
another surprising discovery -it
seems to be possible, at least
on the older 128K machines, to
SAVE and LOAD simple strings in
128K! For instance, if you type
LET a$="test", where a$ is just
an ordinary,undimensioned string
then SAVE "name" DATA a$(), NEW
or reset and (again, without any
DIM) LOAD it in with LOAD "name"
DATA a$(), it seems to work!

I find, however, it only works
with tape and Ramdisk - it
wouldn't work using +D disk.
(Presumably because the +D's
operating system wasn't designed
with this in mind.) I don't know
why such a feature isn't
documented in the +2 manual as
it could be quite useful.

It certainly isn't possible in
48K. Does it work in +3 BASIC?

I read with interest your reply
to Barry Edgeway regarding the
use of opentype files. As a new-
comer to disk systems, this had
been puzzling me too. Although
the +D manual does give the syn-
tax, I still don't understand
how to set up and use such a
file and would be grateful if
you could perhaps explain in
greater detail. Also, you said
they were usually but not always
text files. What other things
besides text can they be used
for?Also mentioned in the manual
are 'microdrive' files and
'special' files. I haven't a
clue what they are either but am
intrigued and curious to know.

In your reply to T. Freeman's
letter you asked if any other
readers had the DTP pack working
with a Multiprint. Well, until I
got my +D I had been using a
Multiprint for years and can
confirm it works perfectly
with the DTP pack. No POKEs or
alterations are necessary, so I
do not understand why he has a
problem. It needs no special
initialisation except a BASIC
'REM mp' command to turn
linefeeds and/or tokens on/off.


Still on the subject of the DTP
pack, I have a useful POKE for
WORDMASTER. You can increase the
number of drives WORDMASTER can
use by POKEing 54631..

Finally, a few things regarding
the +D. Are +D owners aware that
the POKE @ command can actually
work as a double POKE? You could
use it as such to double POKE
Spectrum memory, provided you
subtract the offset 8192. A
simple DEF FN would take care of
that, e.g.
10 DEF FN p(a)=a-8192
20 POKE @ FN p(30000),65535
...would POKE 255 into locations
30000 and 30001.

The form SAVE d1"name"CODE x,y,z
is useful for screen-resident
utilities, e.g. Ram-manager,
Utility 1, Utility 2 etc. (You
can prevent auto-execution of
code by specifying a 'harmless'
third address on loading, e.g.
LOAD d1"name" CODE x,y,56.)

Now for a problem which is caus-
ing me some concern...

I notice if you press BREAK when
the +D is printing, you are
always returned to BASIC with
the 'BREAK requested' message -
even if you had been printing
from machine code!


Does anyone know how to make the
+D simply return control to a
program's own BREAK-handling
routines in these circumstances?
This causes problems with WORD-
MASTER (text files are lost when
you re-run) and I expect would
even cause a crash in a program
if the system variables etc.
were overwritten.

If anyone has succeeded in
patching the system file to do
this, I would be especially
grateful for their details.
(Please print my address as I
would welcome direct replies on
this matter.)

      Regards once again,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

Where possible I shall try to
avoid loading arrays without
first DIMMING them so as to be
compatible with 128K mode but
there are programs that load
string arrays as data like a
wordprocessor and the dimensions
are not known!

Surprisingly the old 48K can do
a tape save of a simple string
variable. This is not in the
manual and I wasn't aware of it
until I just tried it.

OPENTYPE files could be used to
store any data in the same way
that a string array could store
graphics data, plot coordinates,
music data - anything.

Detail on using OPENTYPE files
would need a fuller article so I
shall try to do a DRIVECHAT. It
would be better written though
by an enthusiast of such files
(any offers?) who uses them more
regularly than I.

Disciple and +D "microdrive"
files were specially set up to
put all the varios microdrive
files on disc as one type that
could be accessed by a special
routine but we have always been
mystified as to why. Perhaps it
was to make it easier to trans-
fer files to disc.

"SPECIAL" files have no special
definition but for machine code
programmers to define how they
wish for special purposes.

Using POKE @ as a double poke is
a good idea but remember, it is
non-compatible on any Spectrum
not using the Disciple or +D so
it is more "friendly" to use a
DEF FN to split the high and low
bytes and POKE them separately.

POKE 23728,1 overrides the error
routine but I am not sure if it
will return control to a machine
code routine.
                    - Brian

From: R.S. Hughes, TRURO


Dear Ron and Brian,


It is with regret that I read
about your financial troubles. I
do hope that enough support will
be forthcoming to enable you to
keep on producing OUTLETTERS. I
favour the four pound an Issue
option even though I am an OAP.
I am sure that a lot of us look
forward to a monthly fix of
OUTLET and would like it to be
able to continue in its present
format. The Sinclair & Sam
Computing Magazine recently
disappeared, so I would say to
all, "Don't let OUTLET go!".

I would like to ask for your
help with the Screen Designer
program (Issue 57 May). I think
that the program is top class
and easy to use, however a
problem arises after a screen
has been designed - it is not
possible to SAVE to disk or
tape. On reloading, all that
appears is a blank screen.

            Regards,

              Bob

Brian Cavers to Bob Hughes


Sorry about SCREEN DESIGNER.
We merged in our standard load
and save routines (which work on
any version) but forgot the USR
call which displays the screen
for saving and stores it after
loading! I can't understand how
that one got through our testing
without being spotted!

A corrected version is in this
month's ADD-ENDERS.

                       - Brian.

Firstly, in JOTTER, note the bit in the instructions about each DATA statement starting a new paragraph. To put it the other way, you must start a new DATA statement on a new line each time you start a new paragraph. The Spectrum will not let you (easily) enter text in a BASIC line that is larger than the screen area so the largest paragraph you can have is one screen page.

In Tasword 2, just hold down the symbol key and press the A key to return to the menu where you can select the SAVE TEXT option. You will find Tasword easier to use than JOTTER.

If you have the tape version of Tasword 2 then it will only save the text to tape - not to disc. The prompt will say something like"START THE TAPE,PRESS A KEY" or suchlike. The problem with loading text in COL 80+ and OUTPRINT is due to the following...

Early OUTLET text files had a Sinclair keyword token added at the end called "CODE". This is really a single character that the Spectrum expands into the full word "CODE" just as when you type in 48K BASIC the word appears if you press "I" in extended mode and you can then move the cursor back and forth over the whole word - it does not go through letter by letter as it would in 128K mode.

Later issues of OUTLET use ".#" instead so you need to CAT and enter the name shown.

Чтобы распечатать копию страницы СОДЕРЖАНИЯ (CONTENTS) на версии для +3:

1. RESET
2. Введите `MERGE "CONTENTS"`
3. Подождите несколько секунд, пока не появится «O.K.».
4. Нажмите клавишу ENTER.
5. Наберите: `26 COPY`, затем нажмите ENTER.

Остальным пользователям понадобится собственная программа для дампа экрана. Если вы введете:

```text
SAVE "CONSCRN" SCREEN$
```

По возможности я постараюсь избегать загрузки массивов без предварительного выполнения DIM, чтобы сохранить совместимость с режимом 128K, но ведь есть программы, которые загружают строковые массивы как данные (например, текстовый процессор), и их размеры заранее неизвестны!

Удивительно, но старый добрый 48K действительно умеет сохранять на ленту простую строковую переменную. В руководстве этого нет, и я сам об этом не знал, пока не попробовал только что.

Файлы OPENTYPE можно использовать для хранения любых данных — точно так же, как строковый массив может хранить графические данные, координаты точек (PLOT), музыку — да что угодно.

Подробности использования файлов OPENTYPE потребуют полноценной статьи, поэтому я попробую сделать выпуск DRIVECHAT на эту тему. Впрочем, было бы лучше, если бы ее написал настоящий энтузиаст таких файлов (есть желающие?), который пользуется ими чаще, чем я.

Файлы «microdrive» для Disciple и +D были специально созданы для того, чтобы помещать все различные файлы микродрайва на диск как один тип, к которому можно было получить доступ с помощью специальной подпрограммы, но мы всегда недоумевали, зачем. Возможно, для того, чтобы облегчить перенос файлов на диск.

Файлы «SPECIAL» не имеют специального формата, кроме как предназначенного для программистов в машинных кодах, позволяя им определять его по своему усмотрению для особых задач.

Использование POKE @ в качестве двойного poke — хорошая идея, но помните, что это несовместимо ни с одним Spectrum без Disciple или +D, так что куда более «дружелюбно» использовать DEF FN для разделения старшего и младшего байтов и заносить их через POKE по отдельности.

POKE 23728,1 переопределяет процедуру обработки ошибок, но я не уверен, вернет ли это управление в подпрограмму на машинном коде.
                    — Brian
